1.note: Qoheleth is using **Keep your feet** as a common expression of the culture to mean “be careful about how you conduct yourself.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Watch your conduct]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the temple were **the house of God**, since that was the place where God made his presence known among his people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the temple where God dwells]

2.note: Here, **your mouth** represents what you say. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [concerning what you say]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if your thoughts and intentions were **your heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and do not let your thoughts hurry you]

Here, **to the face of God** represents being in the presence of God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [into the presence of God]

2.q: כִּ֣י הָ⁠אֱלֹהִ֤ים בַּ⁠שָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְ⁠אַתָּ֣ה עַל הָ⁠אָ֔רֶץ
2.note: The implication is that God is exalted far above people and so should be addressed with reverence and with few words. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [For God is exalted in heaven high above you, and you are lowly here on the earth]

3.q: כִּ֛י בָּ֥א הַ⁠חֲל֖וֹם בְּ⁠רֹ֣ב עִנְיָ֑ן וְ⁠ק֥וֹל כְּסִ֖יל בְּ⁠רֹ֥ב דְּבָרִֽים
3.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [For a fool is certainly known by his excessive talking]

3.q: כִּ֛י בָּ֥א הַ⁠חֲל֖וֹם בְּ⁠רֹ֣ב עִנְיָ֑ן וְ⁠ק֥וֹל כְּסִ֖יל בְּ⁠רֹ֥ב דְּבָרִֽים
3.note: Qoheleth is not referring to a specific **dream** or a specific **fool**. He means dreams and fools in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [For some dreams come with much business, and the voice of fools with many words]

Here, **the voice of a fool** represents what a fool says. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and what a fool says]

Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the voice of a fool comes with many words]

4.note: Qoheleth is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [you make a vow]

The implication is that it is God who has no delight in fools who do not fulfill what they have vowed. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for God takes no delight in fools who do not fulfill their vows]

5.note: Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [than that you make a vow but do not fulfill your vow]

6.q: אַל תִּתֵּ֤ן אֶת פִּ֨י⁠ךָ֙ לַ⁠חֲטִ֣יא אֶת בְּשָׂרֶ֔⁠ךָ
6.note: Qoheleth is using **Do not give your mouth to cause your flesh to sin** as a common expression of the culture to mean “do not let what you say bring guilt upon you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Do not let what you say bring guilt upon you]

Qoheleth is using **your flesh** to represent your whole self. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [yourself]

The phrase **the messenger** could mean: (1) the priest who came to collect what a person had vowed to give to God. Alternate translation: [the priest who comes to collect your offering] or (2) an angel sent by God. Alternate translation: [the angel]. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers.
The pronoun **it** refers to the vow that the person made and did not fulfill. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [that your vow was an unintentional sin]
Here, **your voice** represents what you have said. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your words]

Here, **the deed of your hands** represents what you have worked to accomplish. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the work you have accomplished]

7.q: כִּ֣י בְ⁠רֹ֤ב חֲלֹמוֹת֙ וַ⁠הֲבָלִ֔ים וּ⁠דְבָרִ֖ים הַרְבֵּ֑ה
7.note: Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [For there is futility in many dreams and vaporous things and many words]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if things that are empty and fleeting were **vaporous things**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and empty, fleeting things]

8.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **extortion** and **robbery**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [poor people being extorted and just and fair treatment being denied]

The phrase **justice and equity** expresses a single idea. The word **equity** tells more about **justice**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [justice]

The phrase **for a high one over a high one is watching** could mean: (1) that each official is protected by another official who is more powerful than he is. Alternate translation: [for over each official is a higher official who protects him] or (2) that God watches over all of them. Alternate translation: [for over each official is a higher official and God watches over all] You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers.

9.note: Qoheleth is using the possessive form to describe a **profit** that is characterized by coming from **a land**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And the profit that comes from a land]

The expression** it is taken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [everyone takes it]

The expression **is served** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But a field provides for a king]

The implication is that even a king depends on what farmland produces, although it is also possible that Solomon means that a king who promotes farming benefits everyone in his land. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [But even a king depends on what the fields produce]

10.note: Here, **silver** represents money. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [A lover of money will not be satisfied with money]

Qoheleth is not referring to a specific **lover of silver**. He means anyone who loves wealth. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Anyone who loves silver]

Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and whoever loves increase will not be satisfied with income]

11.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if using up a person’s wealth were **eating** it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ones spending it increase]

11.q: וּ⁠מַה כִּשְׁרוֹן֙ לִ⁠בְעָלֶ֔י⁠הָ כִּ֖י אִם ראית עֵינָֽי⁠ו
11.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that the owner of such wealth gains no real advantage from it. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And so its master gains no advantage from it except to look at it with his eyes!]

Qoheleth is using **the sight of his eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “looking at what he owns.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [looking at what he owns]

12.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if restful and satisfying sleep were **Sweet**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The worker sleeps peacefully]

Qoheleth is not referring to a specific **worker**. He means workers in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [is the sleep of any worker]

Qoheleth is referring to all the amounts that a worker might eat by naming two major components, **however little** and **however much**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [whatever amount he eats]

12.q: וְ⁠הַ⁠שָּׂבָע֙ לֶֽ⁠עָשִׁ֔יר אֵינֶ֛⁠נּוּ מַנִּ֥יחַֽ ל֖⁠וֹ לִ⁠ישֽׁוֹן
12.note: Qoheleth is speaking of **the satisfaction of a rich person** as if it were a living thing that could keep him from sleeping. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but a rich person is so full that he cannot sleep]

13.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the misfortune that he saw were a disease, calling it **sickening**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly here and in verse 16. Alternate translation: [a distressing misfortune]
See how you translated **under the sun** in 1:3. This also occurs in verse 18.

The expression **kept** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Wealth that its master keeps, to his harm]

14.note: The implication is that this man had nothing left to leave to his son. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And he had fathered a son, but he had nothing left to leave him]
Here, **in his hand** represents in his possession. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [among his possessions]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:13.

15.note: Qoheleth is referring to dying in a polite way by using the phrase **he will go again**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [naked he will die and depart, just as he came]

Qoheleth is using **naked**, which describes a person who has no clothing, to represent a person who has no possessions at all. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with nothing at all]

16.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that such a person gains nothing at all from his work. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And there is no profit at all for him who toils for the wind!]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **profit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And how does the one who toils for the wind benefit]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the results of such a person’s work were **the wind**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [who toils for something he cannot keep]

17.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the gloom and misery in which such a person lives were **darkness**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all his days he eats his meals in misery]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **vexation**, **sickness**, and **anger**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [and being greatly vexed and feeling sick and being angry]

18.note: Qoheleth is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Consider]
See how you translated the similar expression in 4:4.
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:3.
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:22.

19.q: כָּֽל הָ⁠אָדָ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן ל֣⁠וֹ הָ⁠אֱלֹהִים֩ עֹ֨שֶׁר וּ⁠נְכָסִ֜ים
19.note: Here the masculine term **him** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [each person, whether man or woman, to whom the God gives wealth and possessions]

19.q: וְ⁠הִשְׁלִיט֨⁠וֹ לֶ⁠אֱכֹ֤ל מִמֶּ֨⁠נּוּ֙ וְ⁠לָ⁠שֵׂ֣את אֶת חֶלְק֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠לִ⁠שְׂמֹ֖חַ בַּ⁠עֲמָל֑⁠וֹ
19.note: The implication is that the ability to enjoy wealth is itself a gift that God must give, since not everyone whom God makes wealthy is able to enjoy what he has. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and, though he does not do this for everyone he makes wealthy, has additionally enabled him to eat from it and to accept his portion and to rejoice in his toiling]

The pronoun **this** refers to the ability to enjoy wealth and possessions, although it is also possible that it refers to the wealth and possessions themselves. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [this ability, it is a gift of God]

20.q: כִּ֚י לֹ֣א הַרְבֵּ֔ה יִזְכֹּ֖ר אֶת יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֑י⁠ו
20.note: The implication is that such a person does not brood over how short and troubled his life is. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [For such a person does not dwell on how short and troubled his life is]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **joys**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with things that make him rejoice in his heart]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if a person’s inner feelings were **his heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with the joyful feelings he has inside]
